title: Where Nothing Hurts
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Isaiah saw a brand new world,
With skies all fresh and new;
The old sad things were gone for good,
And only gladness grew.

[Chorus]
The wolf and lamb will eat as friends,
The lion nibble hay;
And nothing hurts on all His hill,
He makes it safe to stay.

[Verse 2]
No sound of weeping in the streets,
No crying anywhere;
Just houses built and gardens grown,
And fruit enough to share.

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
The big dog barked, and Scout stood still,
Then crouched and held a hand;
The dog leaned in, and peace grew up
Where fear had made its stand.

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
So picture lamb and wolf as friends,
Both safe out in the sun;
Heavenly Father's making it,
A world for everyone.

[Chorus]
mood: Open-meadow music. A slow, easy walk under the voice, like a child and a lamb crossing a field in full daylight with nothing to run from. A small celtic harp picks out each step, and a cello holds one warm low note underneath, never moving faster than the walk. It stays light and unhurried the whole way through, and ends out in the sun, settled and glad.
